components.notes: The Cardputer-Adv documentation names its core module Stamp-S3A. The carrier sheet draws it as M1, footprint STAMP-S3-DIP-1.27, with Header 17 (P1) and Header 11 (P2) beside it. The module's sheet titles its pin block STAMP-S3M. specs.cpu: Xtensa 32-bit LX7 dual-core, up to 240 MHz
specs.strapping_note: Strapping pins (datasheet Table 3-1): GPIO0 weak pull-up, GPIO3 floating, GPIO45 and GPIO46 weak pull-downs. GPIO0 and GPIO46 pick the boot mode (GPIO0 low and GPIO46 low: download boot), GPIO45 the VDD_SPI voltage (low: 3.3 V, unless an eFuse forces it; Table 3-4). G46 must not be pulled high before the chip boots. The bench unit's ROM printed boot:0x2b, read with the TRM's GPIO_STRAP_REG bits: GPIO0 latched 1, GPIO45 and GPIO46 latched 0 with the codec on G46.

With Q3 off, the charger's path to the cell crosses Q3's body diode (drain to source), a diode drop below the TP4057's regulated output; the vendor asks for the switch on while charging. Q1 sits between VBAT_IN (drain) and VBAT_OUT (source) with its gate on the CN809J's RESET output.

connects_to.notes: ESD D6, D7 PESDNC2FD3V3B on the signals, D8 PESDNC2FD5VB on VCC, C14 100 nF. The vendor's driver library uses G1 as the external SCL and G2 as SDA. The sheet's net names are GI and GO. The vendor's pin map gives the wire colors: black GND, red 5V, yellow G2, white G1.

Numbering and function names as the vendor's pin map prints them on 2026-11-16 (odd pins left, even pins right). The sheet's symbol numbers the same pins differently (1 RESET G3, 2 INT G4, 3 BUSY G6, 4 SCK G40, 5 MOSI G14, 6 MISO G39, 7 CS G5, 8 GPS-TX G15, 9 GPS-RX G13, 10 SCL G9, 11 SDA G8, 12 5VOUT, 13 GND, 14 5VIN). The vendor page printed on 2026-04-07 names pin 12 (G13) UART_RX and pin 14 (G15) UART_TX, the reverse of today's page; the sheet's GPS-RX on G13 agrees with today's G13 UART_TX. SCK, MOSI and MISO are the microSD's bus, SDA and SCL the internal I2C bus.

components.notes: Drawn on the carrier's power sheet; the vendor page does not say what plugs into it.

specs.function: bidirectional ESD protection on signal lines

components.notes: Carrier: D4 (EN), D5 (G0), D6, D7 (Grove signals), D9-D12 (microSD signals). Module: D1 (GPIO0), D2 (VDD_3V3), D3, D4 (USB data).
Carrier: D8 (Grove VCC), D13 (+3.3V at the microSD). Module: D14 (VIN_5V).

absent.notes: The ESP32-S3FN8 has no in-package PSRAM, and no PSRAM part is drawn on either sheet; the vendor's specification table lists flash only.
No RTC part on any of the five sheets; the ESP32-S3's 32 kHz crystal pins carry the GPIO15/GPIO16 nets.
Power is a TP4057 charger, discrete MOSFET switching and three separate DC-DC converters; no PMIC is drawn.
The battery is read only through the G10 divider.
No touch part is drawn or listed.
The USB-C connector goes straight to the ESP32-S3's native USB pins (GPIO19, GPIO20).
Sound is the ES8311 + NS4150B + 8 ohm speaker path; no buzzer is drawn or listed.
No GNSS part on the board; the EXT header's G13/G15 pins are named GPS-RX/GPS-TX on the sheet for an add-on.
No radio besides the ESP32-S3's is drawn or listed.
The motion sensor is the 6-axis BMI270 only.

notes: Two boards make the product: the Stamp-S3A core module (SoC, crystal, antenna, 3.3 V buck, LCD and RGB LED supply switch, USB-C) and the Cardputer-Adv carrier (charger, power path, boost and buck converters, keyboard, IMU, audio, IR, microSD, Grove, EXT header). Designators repeat between the two sheets (U1-U4, D1-D4, J2, J3, R1-R7, C1-C25...), so each module-side designator here carries '(on the Stamp-S3A)'. Rails: +5VIN (USB 5 V via the module's fuse), VBAT_IN (charger output and switched cell), VBAT_OUT (after Q1, or +5VIN through D1), +5VOUT (SY7088 boost), +3.3V / VDD_3V3 (SY8089 on the carrier and JW5712 on the module, one net), BL_3V3 (switched by GPIO38), AVDD/AGND (codec). The base holds magnets and has LEGO-compatible holes.
